newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 1.7 pct in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 1.7 pct in active trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 1.71 percent in active trade on Tuesday as the market's uptrend continued from Monday amid positive mood, brokers said.

"An uptrend has started. This is not a (temporary) reaction, there are serious stock purchases," said Seyfullah Esen from Oki securities. "This uptrend may last for a month and carry the index to 70,000-75-000 range."

The IMKB-100 closed 1,125.81 points higher at a day's high of 66,944.77. It had gained 1.6 percent yesterday after last week's 2.1 percent rise. Trade volume soared to 9.6 trillion ($107 million) lira from 6.9 trillion ($77 million) on Monday.
Brokers said lower yields and a heavy demand in today's 189-day t-bill auction contributed to market morale.
Bankers were expecting the Treasury to extend t-bill maturities and lower yields after it successfully launched the first foreign-currency denominated bond sale to Turkish banks.
Brokers said easing tensions in the Gulf and newly emerging nine-month profit prospects of companies also buoyed the market.
